candidates.source_name: CBCG — Registar platnih institucija i njihovih agenata (Register of Payment Institutions and their Agents)
candidates.why_relevant: Authoritative, legally mandated list of every licensed payment institution in Montenegro plus their branches and agents. Observed entries: MONTENEGRO TRANSFERS DOO, CAPITAL TRANSFER MNE DOO, MONETA MNE DOO, PAYSPOT ME DOO, ALTA PAY GROUP DOO, PRESTOPAY DOO, Business integration and business intelligence d.o.o. This is the master actor list for the payments-buyer landscape and each entity links to a per-institution PDF listing agents (i.e. distribution/partner networks).
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic HTML scrape of the register page + download of the linked per-institution PDFs; diff snapshots monthly to detect new licences, new agents and de-registrations.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search for the CBCG register, then direct fetch of the register page
queries_used: platna institucija Crna Gora registar CBCG platne institucije
Montenegro payment institution e-money institution licence register Central Bank

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Registar institucija za elektronski novac i njihovih agenata (E-money Institutions Register)
candidates.why_relevant: The EMI register is the tripwire for the first e-money licence in Montenegro. Fetched content stated the register currently contains no registered EMI ('U Registru trenutno nema upisane institucije za elektronski novac'), which is itself a high-value structural fact: any future entry signals a brand-new buyer of KYC, wallet, issuing and switching technology.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Low-frequency change-detection watch (monthly) on the page body; alert on any transition from the empty-register statement.
candidates.discovered_via_method: sibling link from the CBCG registers index; direct fetch
queries_used: platna institucija Crna Gora registar CBCG platne institucije

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Registar platnih sistema (Register of Payment Systems)
candidates.why_relevant: Lists licensed payment systems/switches operating in Montenegro. Switching and clearing operators are procurement decision-makers for processing, HSM, instant-payment and settlement technology; the register identifies who holds the operating licence.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly HTML snapshot + diff.
queries_used: platna institucija Crna Gora registar CBCG platne institucije

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Spisak platnih institucija i institucija za elektronski novac kojima je oduzeto odobrenje (revoked authorisations)
candidates.why_relevant: Negative-signal register: exits and licence withdrawals mark churn in the PSP/EMI buyer base and often precede portfolio or agent-network transfers to a competitor — a supplier-relevant event.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly diff alongside the main PI register.
queries_used: platna institucija Crna Gora registar CBCG platne institucije

candidates.source_name: CBCG FinTech Hub
candidates.why_relevant: Dedicated regulator fintech portal (innovation hub / sandbox-style engagement). Expected to name fintech applicants, PSP innovators and partner projects, and to carry the National Fintech Strategy 2025-2029 workstreams — a pointer to future licensed payments buyers before they appear in the registers.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl site sections and any news/publication feed; snowball named companies into the actor map.

candidates.why_relevant: Regulator's own mapping exercise covering banks, MFIs, payment institutions and e-money institutions — a ready-made actor inventory and terminology source for the payments landscape, published by the body that licenses it.

candidates.source_name: Euronet ATMs Montenegro (euronetatms.me) — independent ATM deployer
candidates.why_relevant: Euronet operates as an Independent ATM Deployer in Montenegro with a local-language site (products include mobile ATMs and cash-deposit ATMs). IADs are first-class procurement actors: they buy ATM hardware, cash management, CIT, monitoring and switching independently of banks, and they sign branding/partnership deals with local banks.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Track product/news/locations pages for ATM-fleet expansion and bank branding partnerships; pair with Euronet Worldwide IR releases for market-entry announcements.

candidates.why_relevant: Asseco/Payten's MoneyGet is a second independent ATM network present in Montenegro, with a locations page revealing physical fleet footprint and a partnership model under which banks join the network. candidates.source_name: Pošta Crne Gore — Javne nabavke (procurement) + money services
candidates.why_relevant: State-owned Post is simultaneously the country's largest non-bank payments distribution network (Western Union, Ria, MoneyGram remittances; counter payment services) and a contracting authority that publishes its own tenders. It is also an authorised e-fiscalisation certificate issuer. This is the single highest-value non-bank payments buyer with a public procurement page.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Weekly crawl of the javne nabavke listing; capture tender documents and award notices; separately monitor the money-services pages for changes of remittance partner.

candidates.why_relevant: E-fiscalisation is the adjacent mandate that drives merchant terminal replacement in Montenegro: every VAT taxpayer must report invoices electronically, certificates are issued by authorised bodies (Pošta Crne Gore and CoreIT were named), and vendors bundle fiscal software with POS hardware (e.g. Adeo POS, sekas.me, VG eFiskal). negative_findings.description: The CBCG e-money institutions register was fetched directly and states that no e-money institution is currently entered.
negative_findings.result_summary: No licensed EMI in Montenegro as observed on the register page; the EMI landscape for this cell is currently empty rather than merely undocumented.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Removes an entire assumed buyer category from the current landscape and turns the register into a market-entry tripwire instead of an inventory.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Montenegrin for cash-in-transit / cash-logistics operators serving banks and ATM networks (transport gotovine, obezbjeđenje novca, agencije za zaštitu) and for any register of licensed private security agencies.
negative_findings.result_summary: No CIT operator, industry list, or Ministry of Interior licence register surfaced; results drifted to AML documents and general payment-services pages.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: CIT and cash-cycle operators are a named part of this coverage cell and are procurement counterparties for ATM cash management; the actor set remains unmapped.

negative_findings.description: Local-language search for a specific 2025-2026 Montenegrin bank/PSP announcement of softPOS or a Visa/Mastercard partnership returned only generic product pages, several of them Serbian and Croatian rather than Montenegrin.
negative_findings.result_summary: No datable ME-specific card-scheme or softPOS partnership announcement was located in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Partnership news is the stated primary announcement channel for this cell; failing to reach it via general search means collection must go entity-by-entity (bank/PSP newsrooms, LinkedIn) rather than by broad query.

negative_findings.description: A search for the ICT Cortex member 'POS4.me' returned no company site; results resolved instead to unrelated Montenegrin fiscalisation vendors.
negative_findings.result_summary: POS4.me exists as a cited cluster-member name but its own web presence was not confirmed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Illustrates that local supplier names harvested from cluster write-ups need individual domain resolution and CRPS verification before being treated as live sources.

negative_findings.description: Montenegrin-language queries about acquiring, POS terminals and card processing are heavily contaminated by Serbian, Bosnian and Croatian results because the language terms are near-identical across markets.
negative_findings.result_summary: Majority of hits for 'prihvatanje platnih kartica' and 'POS terminali' were .rs/.hr/.ba domains.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection must constrain by .me TLD or by explicit 'Crna Gora'/'Podgorica' tokens, or the corpus will be dominated by neighbouring markets and produce false attribution.

coverage_gaps.description: Cash-in-transit, cash-centre and ATM cash-management operators in Montenegro are entirely unmapped, as is the licensing register for private security agencies that would list them.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Query the Ministry of Interior (gov.me) for the register of licensed security agencies ('agencije za zaštitu lica i imovine'), and check bank annual reports and CEJN awards for named CIT contractors.

coverage_gaps.description: The card-processing layer for Montenegro was not resolved: it is unclear which processors (in-house bank platforms, regional processors, or group processors of foreign bank parents such as OTP/CKB, NLB, Erste, Addiko, Ziraat) issue and acquire for each institution.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Read each bank's annual report and card general terms for the named processor, and check the CBCG Register of Payment Systems plus Payten/Nexi/other regional processor reference lists.

coverage_gaps.description: The CEJN procurement portal's tender and award listings were identified but not queried with payments-specific keywords, so it is unknown whether it exposes structured search, CPV filtering, or an API.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a structured probe of cejn.gov.me/tenders with terms bankomat, POS terminal, platne kartice, platni promet, gotovina, procesiranje; document pagination, filters and any machine-readable endpoint before building a collector.

coverage_gaps.description: No Montenegro-specific tender aggregator or paid procurement-alert service was identified as an alternative to the state portal.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Test regional aggregators (e.g. TED for EU-funded ME notices, regional Balkan tender-alert vendors) and record licensing/ToS terms for redistribution.

coverage_gaps.description: Partnership and supplier-selection announcements for ME payment actors likely live on LinkedIn and Facebook company pages rather than websites (Montenegro Transfers was observed publishing WU pricing on Facebook), but no social-channel inventory was built.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a per-actor social-handle registry for licensed PIs, ATM operators and ICT Cortex fintech members, and assess ToS-compliant monitoring options.

coverage_gaps.description: The World Bank TIPS-clone/SEPA modernisation project was identified only via a press release; the project ID, procurement plan and any published contract awards were not retrieved.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Locate the project record on projects.worldbank.org and pull its procurement plan and STEP contract-award notices, which name winning suppliers for payments infrastructure.

brief: Montenegro's payments-buyer landscape is small, register-transparent at the top and announcement-driven below it: the CBCG maintains authoritative registers of payment institutions and their agents (seven PIs observed, including Montenegro Transfers, PaySpot ME and Alta Pay Group), of payment systems, and of revoked authorisations, while the e-money register is presently empty — making it a market-entry tripwire rather than an inventory. Independent ATM deployment is a genuinely separate landscape here, with at least two non-bank fleet operators present (Euronet with a Montenegrin-language site, and Asseco/Payten's MoneyGet), and Pošta Crne Gore doubles as the largest non-bank payments distribution network and a contracting authority that publishes its own tenders. Formal demand signals concentrate in the CEJN e-procurement portal and in the World Bank-financed SEPA/TIPS-clone modernisation project, whose IFI procurement rules will expose supplier awards that domestic partnership deals never do. The weak flank is everything cash-side and processing-side: CIT operators, cash-centre contractors and the actual card processors behind each ME bank remain unidentified, and local-language queries need .me or 'Crna Gora' constraints because Serbian and Croatian results otherwise dominate.
